Question: As a surgeon, have you opened somebody up only to realise that they were beyond saving?
Answer: Unfortunately, yes. There was this patient, 55 year old guy. He came with acute abdominal pain. The patient was in severe distress and the vitals weren’t good even at presentation. He was way too unstable to get a CT scan so we went ahead with just an Ultrasound. Ultrasound wasn’t very conclusive but it suggested intestinal obstruction. The patient was just getting worse and worse so we gave him initial resuscitation and decided to open him. We were prepared to face unexpected scenarios. But we weren’t prepared for what it actually was. As soon as we entered the abdominal cavity, copious amounts of reddish liquid oozed out. A little deeper and there it was..about 80% of his stomach, duodenum, the entire small intestine a portion of ascending and transverse colon were almost black in colour. Every surgeon’s arch nemesis…Superior Mesentric Artery thrombosis. But in this case Stomach was also involved. Basically, the blood supply to his stomach and his entire small intestine and parts of large intestine was compromised. Due to this the parts were ischaemic. There is nothing you can do in this situation. If there was enough healthy gut remaining we would have just cut out the dead part and anastomosed the healthy parts. There just wasn’t enough healthy gut here. So we just closed the patient up, informed the relatives and sent the patient back to the ICU where he passed away a few hours later, surrounded by his family. It’s very disheartening for a surgeon to accept there’s nothing you can do for the patient in front of you. But then, a good surgeon knows when to cut but the best ones know when not to. Just operating when we knew he wouldn’t survive the procedure would have led to him dying on the table. Atleast by closing him up he could pass away surrounded by his family. And believe me, that matters. That matters to the patient and that matters to the family. And while I was heartbroken at losing my patient, it gave me the tiniest bit of satisfaction knowing that we could give that family the last few hours with him. And, hopefully, we could give them closure. P.S. So, a lot of you are interested in the risk factors and how to diagnose the condition. Here’s an article that explains SMA thrombosis is simple terms by Eduardo Franca; Maxim E. Shaydakov; Jason Kosove.

Question: Why do you think most relationships fail?
Answer: Good relationships are not built by being together in good times, the ones that last are the ones where people stick together in the bad times. For me, that is why relationships fail. When we get into relationships, we forget that it’s not all sunshine and rainbows. There are going to be bad times because Hello! Welcome to the real world. But bad times by themselves don’t mean a bad relationship. We need to not give up in the bad times. We need to especially stick together in the bad times. Often, we take the easy way out. Because giving up is just way easier. What is not easy is sitting together and talking about the unpleasant, finding a solution no matter how messy, helping the other person get back on their feet, catching your partner from falling because we all slip up sometimes! If you can help each other in bad times, you’re going to get your forever! Don’t give up on your love because things get tough. Stay together, fight together, help each other out. Sometimes you’ll be the one needing help too and you’re going to want your partner to be their for you too! Most relationships fail because they give each other good times but give up in the bad times! Don’t give up on each other! Remember why you love your person!

Name: Siya Patil
Question: Does anyone want to write their heart out here?
Answer: I want to. I need to. I'm in horrible pain. I lost a patient today. I mean, our unit lost a patient today. I admitted him in the casualty, I was the one who talked to his family, I was also the one who wrote his death certificate. I know my job comes with the responsibility of dealing with death. But what if you think that death is your fault? What if I was more cautious? What if I had suggested more aggressive treatment? What if, what if, what if? He just looked so fine. No distress, no pain and suddenly he went into shock. Neither me, nor any of the consultants thought of anything this serious. Medical science is a mystery and sometimes it throws such googlies. Mistakes happen. But I just hate the fact that my mistakes can kill people. I am aware I'm not senior enough or powerful enough yet to take any vital decisions about patient care. But even then, I can't help but wonder about all the things I could have done differently. Would they have made a difference? Who knows. May be, maybe not. We'll never know. A doctor's day is full of little joys when some patient gives a thank you note or just a smile of gratitude. But what about a bad day? Why isn't this taught in med school? What happens when things go wrong? How do you get back to work the next day when you wake up feeling like a murderer? You just do. You get humbled by the realisation that at the end of the day, you're not God. Then you get ready, put on that white coat, and march ahead. Head held high, heart just a little bit broken.

Name: Siya Patil
Question: What's the hardest truth of life?
Answer: Death. Death is the hardest and ultimate truth of life. You can go round and round, sugarcoat it, pretend like you've any control over it but there it remains…the ultimate truth. I am a doctor, I've probably faced death more than other people. But, the realisation of the inevitability of death dawned to me after I lost my beloved grandmother. My aaji, my dad's mom. She was very very close to me. Since my mom is a working woman, my aaji had a lion's share in raising me. She was my mom. All my childhood memories are with her. She was so so proud of me. Even though she was 89, I just never thought she'll actually leave us all. Silly, I know. Naive, for sure. But, when it comes to people you love, do you actually ever want to believe they are not going to be with you forever? Her death was a massive shock to me, it's been 6 months and I still can't get over it. The idea that I will never hear her call me 'baudi' makes me heartbroken. The fact that I may one day forget her voice crushes me. When my grandmother was sick, I kind of downplayed it. I had that arrogance that she'll fight it all, we'll fight it all. My dad's a doctor, so am I and most of our friends. Aaji was so strong, one illness can't do her any harm. But when that unfortunate moment came, none of us could do anything. We just had to see her go. There was no rhyme or reason. There was no coming back from there. As much as I miss her every moment, nothing anyone can do can bring her back. And every single life has to face death, some sooner, some later. But it's inevitable. It's that inevitability of death that makes life so precious. That's where it ends. Life ends in the ultimate truth.. death.

Question: What are the weirdest reasons to reject a prospective bride/groom in an arranged marriage?
Answer: This is about my elder sister. She's a lawyer and has completed visharad in music (it's a degree in classical music/dance that you get after 7 long years of practice). So after she turned 23, my parents started searching for a groom for her. A lot of prospects rejected because she's into music! Seriously! Girls from reputed families don't sing you see! And this isn't even the weirdest reason. There was this one guy. He had done BCom and was working for his father. Which is fine, we had no problem since his family seemed really nice. So my parents and sister went to their city, they had come with like 10 people. Parents and the guy and his brother, sister in law, uncles and aunts. All of them, at an expensive restaurant obviously at my parents' expense. My sister has glasses, so do I. But that day she was wearing lenses. But she didn't think it is a big deal so while she was talking with that guy at another table she mentioned it to him. My parents and sister came home. They dint really like the family much, a bit too orthodox compared to my family. They called us back after a couple of days. They rejected my sister. Reason- she has glasses! What?! I mean, what?! Apparently they din't want their future grandchildren to have glasses! And his father told this to my father. My father is an ophthalmologist! Genetics is one of a million other causes for short sightedness. Baba told this to his father, also said we're not interested either! He somehow calmly cut the call. Of all the weird reasons I have heard, this seemed really really shallow. I mean, this was 2011 not 1900s! Plot twist - I came across his FB profile a few days back (hence this answer), there was a picture of him, his wife (with apparently a perfect eyesight!) and son. The son was around 3–4 years old with a very cute pair of glasses!

Question: What is it like to be raised by an Indian/Pakistani mother?
Answer: It's the best feeling in the world! You can rest assured you'll always have one person who'll think you're the best no matter what! She'll be over protective, over bearing at times but you'll always, ALWAYS be the best person in the world for her! Like if you get wet in the rain, she won't blame you for not carrying an umbrella; she'll blame the rain! No matter how old you get, you'll always be her baby! You can be a doctor, engineer, lawyer or a prime minister but for her, you'll always be the kid who she read stories to at night! She's your nurse, her remedies always trump those from a prescription! (I am a doctor, but everytime I have a cold I ask my Aai for one of her kadhas!) She's your friend, your secret keeper and own personal cheerleader! She's your shrink, she'll know what you're feeling with a simple hello on the phone! I went through a rough patch for a couple of years. I couldn't clear my pg entrance for a seat of my choice. Everyone, myself included, had given up on me. Except my Mom. Year after year, exam after exam, she didn't stop believing in me. Every time, she would wish me luck, sit outside the exam hall praying and never ever did she ask how my paper went. She never asked what the result was. She knew I would tell her if I had any good news. She never lost hope. She never doubted my abilities. She was there when I cried, she was there when I went into depression, she was there when I couldn't read even one more page cz it was just too much. She never asked me to look for a job or take a branch I don't like. So now, when I finally got the branch I desired (general surgery!) She's there to celebrate it with me! I can proudly say, Aai I am so glad I have you as my mom. Thank you for believing in me when no one else did. And I am privileged to prove it to the world that your faith in me was not blind! Every surgery that I'll successfully perform, every life that I'll save (amen!) will be because of a mother who never stopped believing in her daughter. So what's it like to be raised by an Indian mom? Heaven! P.S. Though this question is specifically for an Indian/Pakistani mom, I firmly believe moms everywhere are the same! A mother's love doesn't change with language or religion you see!

Question: Have you ever mistakenly received a text you weren’t supposed to get?
Answer: Well my mistaken text also happens to be one of the most bizarre things I have ever experienced! A few years back, when I was in 2nd year I got a text on my phone, “Hi Pooja, can you please pick up the phone? Everyone is saying you got married but I refuse to believe. I will die if I don't get a reply.” Now my name isn't Pooja (duh!), neither was my roommate's. Someone (let's calling him A) had sent it mistakenly. At first I thought someone is pranking me. But I had just gotten that number, so it could just have been the previous owner's name. I told that person this isn't Pooja and he has texted the wrong number. And then the interesting part began. He called. I didn't pick up because I usually reject unknown numbers. But then he kept calling and calling and calling. I had 28 missed calls from him. And then a new number (let's call him B) started calling. I picked up. B was A's brother. What he told next was heart breaking. B told me, Pooja was A's girlfriend. And she indeed had my number before me. They were in a long distance relationship. Pooja had an accident and lost her life a few days back. And since A's family thought it'll be too hard for him to digest they told him she got married and hence won't talk to him. He asked me if I can chat with A, pretending to be Pooja for a few days till he believes she is actually married. I was shocked. I didn't know if I could believe him. And honestly, I didn't need to get in the mess...patho, micro, pharma were killing me as is! But B was pleading too much and sounded desperate so I gave in. I chatted with him, pretending to be his ex for a few days, till his family broke the unfortunate news. The whole texting with him thing was super weird. I felt guilty but he seemed over emotional and I understood why his family was so cautious. We chatted for a few days till he seemed to accept Pooja won't be in his life anymore. Then his brother called me again to inform that they are going to tell him the truth. A stopped texting me after that. He called me a week later to apologise and thank. Turned out this bizzare story was actually true. Life is, sometimes, weirder than your imagination! My naive decision to trust a stranger turned out to be a huge help for some unfortunate young man. It may have been morally questionable, but all the hearts were definitely in the right place. We continued to stay in touch over the years. He called me didi! That was one wrong message that I am glad I received. Edit- to everyone commenting this is fake, I take it as a compliment. Also, All said and done, you may believe it or you may not but thank you for reading!

Question: What can make my skin glow naturally?
Answer: As someone who struggled for years with acne and horrible dry patches (yup, the lethal combination!) I finally have good skin. Though I still get a few stubborn breakouts here and there, I mostly have a quite plain, glowy skin now. So after trying a million different ways and means for years, these are the things that worked for me. Now I'll get into the natural products that worked for me. African black soap- This soap is traditionally made in Africa with Shea Butter, oat kernels, rosemary, and various leafs and herbs. Though the original form is available online, I prefer a little modified version that is less harsh on the skin from brands like Shea Moisture and Equate beauty. Trust me guys, this soap is MAGIC. Initially it might flare up the acne but on regular use (froth it it up and apply the froth on your face. Wash off with warm water after 2–3 mins) it clears up your skin like nobody's business. It has also significantly reduced my acne marks. I am using this brand these days. But I have also used Shea Moisture and Nubian beauty in the past and all work the same more or less! Essential oils- now this is a very exciting find. I was quite apprehensive about applying oils directly to my face but the right oils can enhance your skin just so much. Some of the combinations that I use are jojoba oil with a few drops of ylang ylang oil, jojoba oil with tea tree, olive oil with lemon oil, olive oil with lavender. Here the first oil acts as a carrier, so use 4–5 drops and the second oil is potent, to be used like a drop or 2. Apply them before sleeping, your skin with be glowy and supple the next morning! This is the brand of essential oils that I have been using. I got them from Amazon and have used up quite a few. Face pack- face pack gives a very deep cleanse to the skin. There are a variety of natural face packs available that suit all the different skin type. But for oily skin, I prefer Aztec clay (available on Amazon), Charcoal masks, the oldie Goldie multani mitti or Fuller's earth. You can take them a little further by adding turmeric, sandalwood powder, aloe vera and apple cider vinegar. Also a simple mask of honey and a few drops of lemon juice can give you that instant glow. So basically, this is how I keep my skin glowy and healthy. It may seem extensive but it's actually quite basic. But maintaining your skin isn't an overnight thing. It takes patience but it's worth it !

Question: What does depression look like?
Answer: What does it look like? A sad, teary eyed girl sitting in a filthy room with papers scattered around the room and a half eaten pizza? Or an unkept young man, overgrown beard surrounded by empty beer cans and cigarette butts? Ha! If only it was that simple. Depression is also that girl who always keeps smiling, that boy who keeps cracking jokes. That doctor who drives a Ferrari. Or that actress who just won an Oscar. Depression looks like all of the above. We ofter relate depression with the simplistic outwardly sad appearance we see in the movies. But appearances are Often deceiving. Which is why we often miss the obvious depression in people all around us. We need to start actually seeing people than just looking at them. We need to see beyond the smiles. We need to listen more. Sometimes a loud laugh is just a cry for help. This is me in my worst phases of depression, at Disneyland, the happiest place on earth! Ironic, isn't it? This is me today, after a very long work day, in dull old hospital scrubs. Well kept? Naa. Happy? You bet! My point is, depression doesn't look like a textbook presentation. Sure, many patients will fit that bill. But many won't. And we need to be aware of that.

Question: What are some funny stories from your college days?
Answer: College days! It hasn't been that long and it already seems a lifetime ago! I studied in Mumbai. Seth GS Medical College! I lived in a hostel. I had my girl gang to hang out with. We lived together, studied together, went out together. And it was just so much fun! Outside the hospital, we were just a bunch of silly 19–20 year olds enjoying aamchi Mumbai! So on one of those outing me and my 4 girl friends went to Colaba. It has a huge Street market. So after wasting an unjustified amount of money and energy on buying things we definitely didn't need, we went to Theobroma. It is a kind of a dessert and chocolate shop. Its pretty famous and pretty old. It is most famous for its chocolate brownies and rum chocolates. Its display usually looks like this (Image source- Google) (I am already drooling!) So as we were sitting there, gossiping and eating brownies my friend, who knew I don't drink, dared me to eat a dozen rum chocolates. I had never even had a beer, let alone rum, but I went ahead anyway. So I ordered a box of rum chocolates and took a teeny tiny bite. As yummy as it was, it had a strong punch of rum. I kept eating till the very last one. Now, they are in no way strong enough to actually make you drunk but I guess it had more of a psychological effect on me. Or maybe it did affect me since I don't drink. But in any case, I felt drunk! So when we walked back to the local station I was slightly tipsy. We got in the train, next stop was Marine drive. I suddenly had the crazy idea to get down and go to the beach. Ofcourse none of my friends agreed since it was already 10 and my hostel had a curfew of 11. As we debated, the train started moving. Without even thinking I jumped out of the train. And BAAAMMMM. I fell face flat on a crowded Marine lines station. A small crowd gathered around me, as I regained my senses I looked around and asked, “Where are my shopping bags!?” I could hear people laughing at me. Who thinks of shopping bags on waking up from a fall?? Me, that's who! The train was super slow, so I wasn't hurt but I was super embarrassed. I narrated this whole scene the next morning, and was ridiculed for weeks for getting drunk on rum chocolates! P. S. Jumping from or getting in moving trains is incredibly reckless and highly dangerous. Please do not, ever, try it. I was lucky to get out unscratched. Not everyone comes out with a laugh.

Question: What is it like to fail in medical entrance examinations (AIPMT, CET, NEET)? What alternative path would you choose and why?
Answer: I was a topper throughout school. For 11th and 12th I was given free admission in all coaching classes. Everyone was sure I'll get through the entrance. I was too. Then came the result day, I did not make it. I knew the average rank to get in and I missed it by 2 marks. What hurts more than a pathetic score? Missing it by 2–3 marks. I faced that. To say my parents were disappointed is an understatement. It was unimaginable. But, medicine was a passion. There was no plan B for me. So I took a drop. I spent the first 5 months repenting my mistakes, crying over my failure. I woke up suddenly 1 day, realised I am about to lose this opportunity too and started studying. 4 months later I gave my exam and when the result came I had scored 198/200 and was rank 3 in my state! The drop year was horrible, but I made it only because I was crazy about the field. But, if you don't think this is your passion, search for it. Medical isn't the only option. You can go for physiotherapy, dentistry, pharmacy, fashion design, architecture…the possibilities are endless! Just listen to your heart and put in everything you have to achieve your dream. If you do something just because people expect you to, you'll never be able to excel in it. It's better to be the best in the field of your choice than being a mediocre doctor.

Question: How did your classmates who were not so good in studies turn out in life?
Answer: I had a friend. She wasn't good at studies. As in not in the typical sense. She wasn't good at maths or science or economics. And her rank was way down the double digits. She barely scored 60% in school... And I'm being generous here. She had just one passion though. Literature. She loved reading. LOVED. I am an avid reader myself, but her love for the written word exceeded mine. She always told everyone she wanted to become a journalist. Most people ridiculed her. In 10th boards, she got 56%. Where my mother was kind of unhappy with my 90%, I clearly remember her mother distributing sweets for her 56%. I really felt a little jealous of her at that moment! Our paths changed after 10th. I went for science and eventually medical school. She took up arts. We lost touch for a few years, then one random day as I opened Hindustan Times, there was a really good article. I read it, looked for the author's name. Guess what? It was my friend from school! She really did become a journalist! I felt so so happy for her! She didn't let any condescension stop her. She followed her heart and achieved her dream! Today she's an assistant editor at a leading magazine. So what is my classmate who wasn't good at studies doing now? Living her dream! Follow your passion. Don't let a set of questions or a report card judge you or your talent. Life begins outside the walls of your school. Find what flames your soul and just go for it. It's better to be a badass journalist than a mediocre doctor or engineer! Edit- I am really sorry to everyone asking for my friend's name, even though she was fine with me sharing her story she is not comfortable with giving out her name (understandable).

Question: What disgusts you?
Answer: People. Yeah, some people disgust me. Lies, deceits, manipulation disgusts me. Picture this. You have a friend, a very good friend. A friend who makes you believe just how special you're to him. How much he values your friendship. How much he values you. You think you have a friend for life. Your parents treat him like family. He keeps talking about his fiance and you think he's such a gem of a guy. Such an honest guy, right? Then one fine day, something seems off. You have a fight. You dig a little. You talk to people. And you realise, your friend isn't a friend at all. You realise, he is a serial cheater. Not 1, not 2 but multiple side affairs. And to maintain all those nasty affairs, he has told nothing but lies to you for the past 1.5 years. On top of that, he has been spreading just filthy, filthy lies about you. Ahh. The heartache. The sheer heartbreak. It's like suddenly your eyes open. And you see clearly the sheer amount of filth and evil. You end up feeling just plain stupid. How could you not see through his facade? You remember the instances you ignored, some harmless lies you caught, those moments when his eyes turned cold and dark just for a fleeting moment. You realise you have just wasted your time and feelings. You were played by a sociopath. You never meant anything to him, your friendship meant nothing, because that's how these sociopaths work. And you just end up betrayed and heartbroken. It's like the death of a friend. I can't even write all the things that he has done, cz just thinking about it makes my blood boil. Even after all this, there's this tiny part of your heart that wants to believe maybe, just maybe there's some fragment of goodness in him. Maybe you didn't just trust a total dark soul. But then you're reminded of all the vile, immoral things he has done. And you have to let that tiny part of your heart die. I think, that disgusts me, the murder of that tiny part of your heart that still wants to believe in fairytales..

Question: What is the strangest way you found out your significant other was cheating on you?
Answer: I read his chat live as he was chatting with the other girl! So here it goes, my then boyfriend and I were in long distance then. He was not into social media so I usually maintained his FB account. Replying to messages and changing profile pictures and all. And I guess he forgot I have his password. One fine day I logged into his account, I opened messenger to check new messages and I saw an active chat. I realised he's chatting with someone. Curiosity got the best of me and I started reading the chat. He was chatting with a nurse from his new college. The chat was innocent initially and I was actually happy to see he's making friends in the new place, but very soon it turned into him asking her if she's single. She was. He said he is too, right when I, his girlfriend of 4 years, was reading that chat! Aah. What not did I read. Him telling her she's the most beautiful girl he's ever seen, how he has never felt that love for anyone, how he's always gonna be by her side, how he thinks she's the one for him. Oh, did I mention he complimented her breasts? All in one chat. I called him right away. He cut my call, messaged me that he's in the OT. I told him to say hi to the nurse! He called back immediately, followed by days of denial, then acceptance then begging. Funnily enough, we dint break up immediately after that. It took me 6 more months to gain enough courage and sanity to break up and move on.

Question: What was the last text message you sent to your ex?
Answer: Believe it or not, I sent a poem I wrote for him in the last message. It was the the last poem I ever wrote for him and I sent it 3 days back, almost 3 years after we broke up. I realised I am ready for a closure now and so sent him the poem. It is incredibly cheesy and romantic, but so am I! Here it is, (I can put it out publicly now since it doesn't hold any emotional attachment for me anymore. I rarely, if ever, publish my poems!) HIRAETH You took all the trouble to walk away from me, So tell me old friend, How's the view from that distance? Do you see now what I begged you to see when you were here? Do you see the ruins of a dead romance? Do you see the mistakes we made? Do you hear the words left unsaid? Tell me old friend, How's the view from that distance? Do I look beautiful from there atleast? Do I seem to have fixed my broken heart piece by piece? Do you see me smiling again, unbroken? Tell me old friend, How's the view from that distance? Do the scars, yours and mine, hurt less from there? Do you see me, sometimes, spiralling down the past unaware? Do you see me moving on, daring to, yet again, care? Tell me old friend, How's the view from that distance? Do you ever just want to reach out and touch my smile? Do you wish you had stayed awhile? Do you ever feel like coming back, If you only to tell me why you left? Do you ever, for a moment, regret? Edit- a few of you asked about what happened after this. Well, actually I din't send the message for anything to happen. It was a closure message. So even if he had initiated anything I would have stopped it right there. But, he just replied back saying sorry and how he didn't deserve me. I said, “yeah you're right!” And that was it! We haven't talked since. PC- pinterest

Question: At what moment did you realize you were finally over someone you used to love?
Answer: When I forgot to wish him on his birthday! Well his birthday falls on 25th December, so it's especially hard to miss. Even after our break up I wished him every year at midnight, without fail. Last year, I totally forgot. I actually remembered 2 days later when I called another friend of mine for her birthday. As it dawned on me, I realised I hadn't just forgotten his birthday, I had actually forgotten 4 years of experiences, 4 birthdays I spent with grand pre planning and surprises, 4 years of love, laughter, hurt and that singular moment of crushing heartbreak. I am a pretty nice person, I never miss an opportunity to wish anyone on their birthday. But this missed one meant just so much to me! Icing on the cake? When I decided to call him for a belated wish, I couldn't remember his phone number! I just smiled a little after this!After 2 years, I had finally deleted his number from my mind (had deleted from my phone 15 months prior to this!) After this long and lonely journey, I had finally moved on. I had stopped loving him. That was the single most liberating moment of my life. I was free!

Question: Do doctors think and worry about their patients when they get home, or do they only see them as “work” and forget about them at the end of the day?
Answer: Thanks for the A2A. I can't speak of all doctors but only for myself. I think of my patients when I get home, I worry about some that I know are not doing well. I celebrate the ones that were especially tricky but were successful cases! I think of all those things. Patients who said things especially touching, who were too poor and we couldn't help, who were gone too far off for us to help. All things good and bad. I don't know if this is healthy though. I have spent many a sleepless nights over patients we lost, I've invested way too many emotions on patients' stories. And eventually, it takes a toll on you. So I'm learning to detach myself a little. Trying to be professional more! I'm still an infant in the world of surgery but as I grow, I hope I can maintain my empathy but also protect myself!

Question: At what age did you get married? Are you happy about being married at that age?
Answer: I got married at 29. A little old by Indian (and my mom’s!) standards. But for me it was the right age, I wanted to be a little settled in my career before getting married. Me and my then boyfriend were already together since 4 years by that point and he was basically just waiting for me to get settled in my career. Thankfully for me, neither my parents nor my boyfriend put any pressure on me to get married earlier. And I’m very thankful for that. Not all girls in India can say that. BUT, am I happy about getting married at that age? Well I’m happy being married to my wonderful husband but I really wish I had done it sooner. It would be so great to have even more time to build our lives together! Now everything seems to have a deadline, buy your own car before you’re 32, kids by 33, house by 35 and so on. We don’t really have time to just slow down and just ‘be’, you know? So like, I’m glad I settled my career first, I just wish i had done it sooner. Everyone, get married only when you’re ready. Not because you’re getting older or everyone else’s getting married or log kya kahenge! Get married because you simply cannot wait to spend the rest of your lives together!
